content: The following is a professional summary of the provided references and declarations of interest, written in clear and concise English: 1. The 2010 Advanced Life Support Resuscitation Guidelines (Chapter 10, pages 106–117) provide updated recommendations for managing critical care scenarios. 2. Rosenbloom et al. (2013) conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials to evaluate whether antipyretics prevent the recurrence of febrile seizures in children. Their findings were published in the European Journal of Paediatric Neurology (Volume 17, pages 585–588). 3. Rosman et al. (1993) performed a controlled trial to assess the efficacy of diazepam administered during febrile illnesses in preventing recurrent febrile seizures. The results were published in the New England Journal of Medicine (Volume 329, pages 79–84). 4. The Royal Children’s Hospital Melbourne (2011) developed clinical practice guidelines for managing afebrile seizures, accessible online. 5. Rutter and Smales (1977) examined the role of routine investigations in children presenting with their first febrile convulsion. Their study was published in Archives of Disease in Childhood (Volume 52, pages 188–191). 6. Sasidaran, Singhi, and Singhi (2012) reviewed the management of acute seizures and status epilepticus in pediatric emergencies, as published in the Indian Journal of Pediatrics (Volume 79, pages 510–517). 7. Shah et al. (2014) developed an evidence-based guideline for pediatric prehospital seizure management using the GRADE methodology, published in Prehospital Emergency Care (Volume 18, Supplement 1, pages 15–24). 8. Shiva and Hashemian (1998) studied the clinical course and diagnostic evaluation of febrile seizures, with findings published in the Journal of the Pakistan Medical Association (Volume 48, pages 276–277). 9. Simoes et al. (2003) investigated the management of severely ill children in sub-Saharan Africa when referral is difficult. Their work appeared in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization (Volume 81, pages 522–531). 10. Singhi et al. (2012) conducted a prospective pilot trial to assess the risk of hypoxemia in patients with severe pneumonia but no initial hypoxemia. The study was published in Paediatrics International Child Health (Volume 32, pages 22–26). 11. Sternowsky and Lagenstein (1981) evaluated the use of phenobarbital in febrile convulsions in children, published in Deutsche Medizinische Wochenschrift (Volume 106, pages 49–51). 12. Stores (1991) explored the contribution of EEG to the management of febrile seizures, as published in Archives of Disease in Childhood (Volume 66, pages 554–557). 13. Strengell et al. (2009) conducted a randomized controlled trial on the use of antipyretic agents to prevent febrile seizure recurrences, published in Archives of Pediatrics & Adolescent Medicine (Volume 163, pages 799–804). 14. Subhi et al. (2009) performed a systematic review on the prevalence of hypoxemia among ill children in developing countries, published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases (Volume 9, pages 219–227). 15. Takanashi et al. (2006) studied diffusion MRI abnormalities following prolonged febrile seizures with encephalopathy, published in Neurology (Volume 66, pages 1304–1309). 16. Teng et al. (2006) assessed the risk of intracranial pathologies requiring emergency intervention after a first complex febrile seizure episode in children, published in Pediatrics (Volume 117, pages 304–308). 17. Thilothammal et al. (1993) evaluated the role of phenobarbital in preventing febrile convulsion recurrences, published in Indian Pediatrics (Volume 30, pages 637–642). 18. Tiamkao and Sawanyawisuth (2009) identified predictors and prognosis of status epilepticus treated with intravenous sodium valproate, published in Epileptic Disorders (Volume 11, pages 228–231). 19. Treiman et al. (1998) compared four treatments for generalized convulsive status epilepticus, published in the New England Journal of Medicine (Volume 339, pages 792–798). 20. Trinka (2009) reviewed the relative value of standard anticonvulsants, including phenytoin, fosphenytoin, phenobarbital, valproate, and levetiracetam, published in Epilepsia (Volume 50, page 403). 21. Trinka et al. (2014) conducted a systematic review on the efficacy and safety of intravenous valproate for status epilepticus, published in CNS Drugs (Volume 28, pages 623–639). 22. Uhari et al. (1995) studied the effects of acetaminophen and low intermittent doses of diazepam on preventing febrile seizure recurrences, published in The Journal of Pediatrics (Volume 126, pages 991–995). 23. Van Stuijvenberg et al. (1998) conducted a randomized controlled trial on ibuprofen syrup administered during febrile illnesses to prevent febrile seizure recurrences, published in Pediatrics (Volume 102, page 51). 24. Verrotti et al. (2004) evaluated the effectiveness of intermittent oral diazepam prophylaxis in febrile convulsions, published in the European Journal of Paediatric Neurology (Volume 8, pages 131–134). 25. Visser et al. (2012) examined the behavioral and cognitive outcomes of febrile seizures in preschool children as part of the Generation R study, published in Developmental Medicine & Child Neurology (Volume 54, pages 1006–1011). 26. Webb et al. (2012) studied treatment failure among Kenyan children with severe pneumonia in a cohort study, published in Pediatric Infectious Disease (Volume 31, pages e152–e157). 27. West et al. (1999) investigated long-term morbidity and mortality following hypoxemic lower respiratory tract infections in Gambian children, published in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization (Volume 77, pages 144–148). 28. White et al. (1988) demonstrated that a single dose of phenobarbital prevents convulsions in cerebral malaria, published in The Lancet (Volume ii, pages 64–66). 29. WHO (2005–2015) published various guidelines and handbooks on emergency triage, assessment, treatment, and management of common childhood illnesses, including febrile seizures and severe acute malnutrition. 30. Yasiry and Shorvon (2014) conducted a meta-analysis on the effectiveness of five antiepileptic drugs in treating benzodiazepine-resistant convulsive status epilepticus, published in Seizure (Volume 23, pages 167–174). 31. Yu et al. (2003) evaluated the safety and efficacy of intravenous valproate in pediatric status epilepticus and acute repetitive seizures, published in Epilepsia (Volume 44, pages 724–726). 32. Zhang et al. (2011) performed a meta-analysis on the accuracy of symptoms and signs in predicting hypoxemia among young children with acute respiratory infections, published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease (Volume 15, pages 317–325). 33.
